exact_claim: The complete supporting-tangent lines actually meeting each of three pairwise disjoint arbitrary convex subsets of R^3 have a spatial union of three-dimensional Lebesgue outer measure zero; nonclosed, unbounded, nonsmooth and lower-dimensional inputs are allowed.
claim_limits: Actual intersection and supporting-plane containment; not mere secancy or closure-only contact.
Pairwise disjoint original sets; closures need not be disjoint.
Not a 2-manifold cover, Hausdorff-dimension-two bound, smoothness or rectifiability theorem.
No global closedness claim for the nonclosed input case.
No first-priority, current-openness or exhaustive-literature certification.
No scientific proof inferred from finite checks.
interesting_result: A third distinct contact forces a quadratic swept-volume determinant to vanish identically; the published two-rectangle example demonstrates positive-volume common tangents for two disjoint sets.
